annotations.text:
A · Sketch grid — the attached sketch, literally.
Two by two at every width, screenshots tilted and broken out of the card top. Reads as a toy shelf.
Tradeoff: at 390px the two-up cards leave ~150px of text width, so the blurbs have to be short — that is the least SEO copy of the three.

B · Marquee row — four abreast, editorial hero.
Left-aligned hero so the h1 and the paragraph read as one block; cards straight-on and equal weight.
Tradeoff: four equal cards say all four tools are equally real. Three of them are not.

C · Featured — the shipped tool leads.
The dex builder gets a split hero card with a real screenshot and a solid CTA; the other three sit in a supporting row.
Tradeoff: it buries the league builder, which is the tool with a settled spec and the next page to rank.

SEO structure, same in all three:
· h1 carries "make your own Pokédex" plus region and league.
· Each card is an <h2> that exactly matches its slug: /custom-pokedex-builder, /pokemon-league-builder, /favorite-pokemon-picker.
· The footer repeats the four links as anchor text.
Watch out: making / a router moves the dex builder off the URL that ranks today (~pos 7.8 for "pokedex builder").

D · Poster cards. Mobile and tablet space out evenly: three equal flex spacers put the same gap above the intro text, between the text and the grid, and between the grid and the footer.
The Hammer is centred between the card's top edge and the top of its heading, so the space above it matches the space below by construction rather than by eye.
Desktop has about 110px between the sub-text and the artwork, which is the room for a hover nudge.

This pass, four changes.
The screenshot shadow no longer stops in a straight line at the card's bottom. The shadow now paints in its own layer that fades out over the last 34px, so it thins to nothing instead of ending on an edge; the screenshots themselves still cut on that edge, which is the point.
Tablet is the packed one: the artwork scales to 82%, so the two rows sit closer. `art` is the single knob, and the left overhang scales with it or the gradient rule fails the build.
Card copy is a step larger — 9.4px title, 8.8px blurb at 390px. It cannot reach the 11.5px of the "No account…" line: "Trainer Card & League Builder" already fills 154 of the 158px the card gives it, so one line of title caps the size at about 9.6px. Matching 11.5px needs a shorter title or one card per row.
Line breaks in the headings and blurbs come from `text-wrap: balance`, not manual breaks.
